project.topic: What if Earth's axis had no tilt?
project.title: What if Earth's Axis Had No Tilt? Your Summer Evenings Vanish
project.audience: Curious international viewers; playful discovery through one familiar barbecue.
project.core_question: Can you rescue a long summer evening by waiting or chasing summer south on a permanently upright Earth?
project.viewer_takeaway: Zero tilt removes long summer evenings and short winter days; equal day length does not equal equal sunlight angle, and eccentricity still varies sunlight.

scientific_model.baseline_reality: Earth has about 23.44 degrees obliquity, a roughly 24-hour solar day and orbital eccentricity 0.0167; seasonal solar declination changes day length and noon sunlight angle.
scientific_model.counterfactual_change: Earth has permanently zero obliquity: its spin axis is normal to its orbital plane. This is an alternative established Earth, not a sudden torque, axis snap, or violent transition.
assumptions: Keep rotation rate, present eccentric orbit, solar output, geography and atmosphere. Keep calendar month names and present January perihelion orientation as storytelling conventions.
The anchor patio is at 45 degrees north; the southern search compares 45 degrees south. All stated hours are LOCAL SOLAR TIME, not civil time or daylight-saving time.
Nonpolar geometric day/night intervals are each half a solar day at zero declination. Solar-disc size and atmospheric refraction extend observed daylight; say roughly twelve hours.
The exact-pole solar center is on the geometric horizon; refraction can lift the visible disc. The equatorial overhead Sun is at solar noon only.
No temperatures, weather, crop yields, ice-sheet extents or climate states are predicted. Existing polar ice is an illustrative surface, not a forecast of new freezing.
Month/hour changes are explicit time jumps or a dinner rescheduling card. The Sun does not suddenly change its physical trajectory.

The orbital view enlarges the Sun and Earth independently and compresses their separation for readability. Body sizes are not a physical comparison; eccentricity, perihelion/aphelion distance ratios and the irradiance ratio are retained.
causal_chain: Zero obliquity fixes solar declination atzero; neither hemisphere tilts toward the Sun.
The rotating day/night boundary gives most latitudes roughly twelve daylight hours, removing long summer days and short winter days.
Waiting or changing hemisphere cannot recover a long summer evening, so the initial plan fails.
Latitude still changes incidence angle: oblique rays spread a fixed incoming beam across more ground. Equal daylight is not uniform solar heating.
Eccentricity changes incident sunlight worldwide together; January perihelion gives about 6.9 percent more incoming flux thanJulyaphelion. This is not a temperature forecast.
The protagonist changes dinner time:17:00 solar-time barbecue has daylight at the chosen latitude inJune andDecember, unlike the initial 20:00 plan.
uncertainties: Climate adjustment, cloud, ocean, atmospheric circulation and ice feedbacks require coupled modeling; no numerical climate claims are made.
The premise suppresses real obliquity variations indefinitely; its dynamic origin is outside scope.
Refraction, terrain and equation of time alter apparent/civil sunrise and sunset; telemetry uses ideal geometric solar time.

claims.statement: Axial tilt produces familiar seasonal changes in sunlight angle and day length.
claims.reasoning: NASA and NOAA describe seasonal hemisphere alternation caused by obliquity; zero obliquity removes that geometric alternation.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Start with an already upright planet; never show a physical axis snap or destruction.

claims.statement: At zero obliquity, nonpolar latitudes have about twelve hours of daylight throughout the year.
claims.reasoning: Solar declination delta=0 gives cos(H 0)=-tan(latitude)*tan(delta)=0 away from exactpoles, soH 0=90 deg and a half-day illuminated interval. Refraction and solar-disc size lengthen visible daylight.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Say roughly, exclude poles in speech, label LOCAL SOLAR TIME; never promise identical observed/civil sunsets.

claims.statement: At 45 degrees north or south, zero tilt removes long summer evenings and short winter daylight intervals.
claims.reasoning: At either chosenlatitude the same geometric half-day interval applies eachmonth.20:00 solar time is dark;17:00 solar time is sunlit. Compare with modern tilt-driven seasons.
claims.presentation_guardrail: The barbecue/search are illustrative personal actions. Winter-afternoon benefit refers to this midlatitude, not polar/equatorial regions.

claims.statement: Equal sunlight duration does not imply equal incoming solar energy per unit ground area at different latitudes.
claims.reasoning: For matched incoming beam and atmosphere, irradiance on horizontal ground follows cosine of incidence angle. Oblique sunlight covers more ground; NOAA explains the latitude effect.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Stage real sunlight direction, grounded post/pergola shadows and oblique ground illumination. Do not invent thermometers, equal local climates or a floating measurement device.

claims.statement: At zero tilt the solar center is overhead at equatorial solar noon and on the geometric horizon at exactpoles.
claims.reasoning: Noon altitude equals 90 degrees minus absolute latitude when declination=0. At either pole altitude remains 0 as azimuth circles; disc size/refraction remain.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Explicitly use noon at equator; polarSun stays nearhorizon, never normal twelve-hour rising/setting arc.

claims.statement: Eccentricity 0.0167 preserves approximately 6.9 percent perihelion-to-aphelion variation in incident solar flux.
claims.reasoning: NASA gives e=.0167 and distances 147.095/152.100 millionkm. Inverse-square flux ratio=((1+e)/(1-e))^2=1.06909. Retained calendar convention puts perihelion aroundJanuary.
claims.presentation_guardrail: This is top-of-atmosphere solar flux, not weather or temperature. Keep orbit nearly circular; do not claimJanuary hottest.

claims.statement: Eccentricity-driven irradiance varies both hemispheres together rather than alternating tilt-driven summers.
claims.reasoning: Sun–Earth distance is shared globally; zero declination preserves geometric equatorial symmetry. Localweather and thermal lag need not match.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Strengthen paired incoming-ray indicators together, not synchronous weather or equal temperatures.

creative_direction.logline: Your late summer barbecue loses its daylight. Waiting and searching the other hemisphere fail, until sunlight geometry reveals the plan that works.
creative_direction.visual_identity: Tactile premium 3 D miniature discovery: a supported grill, calendar, lamp and paving anchor a playful astronomical counterfactual. Return to the same patio with a completed earlier dinner.
creative_direction.lighting: Amber grill/lantern atnight; coherent solar key and restrained skylight byday. Incoming beams illuminate physical ground, without invented temperature colors.
creative_direction.camera_language: Eye-level patio holds preserve prop relationships; globe comparisons earn a scale change. Cuts clarify month, latitude and time transitions; ground sway remains subtle.
creative_direction.motion_language: One-time grill ignition, physical month flip, north-to-south search, real lengthening post/pergola shadows, polar horizon sweep and a completed earlier dinner. Evaluate every state from absolute film time.
creative_direction.world_scale_policy: Ground views use 1 unit=1 metre; Earth and orbit use explicit local planetary units. Do not exaggerate eccentricity or add floating rulers.
creative_direction.opening_hook: A grill ignites under a darkJune 20:00 solar-time sky; the lost long summer evening disrupts dinner.
creative_direction.mid_video_rehook: At22.8s the failed southern search reveals the real distinction: the same hours of sun can arrive at different angles. As the geographical noon view moves toward high latitude, low rays spread light over more ground and a planted post/pergola casts longer shadows.
creative_direction.ending_payoff: Winter short afternoons are gone too. After a marked December 17:00 daylight comparison, the June dinner card changes 20:00→17:00 with a clear edit to an earlier sunlit hour. Waiting for another month cannot rescue the original plan.
creative_direction.loop_connection: The same grill/lantern sound returns with successful dinner in daylight; openingdark 20:00 andclosinglit 17:00 show the changeddecision.
creative_direction.asset_policy: Reuse verified registry assets and Modeling helpers. Only the story-specific grill/calendar/clock, grounded angle proof and nearly circular orbit curve are new.
